sources.excerpt: EarthQuaker Devices Hoof Review: Muff Fuzz with Better Mids Skip to content The Guitar Side Home Gear Reviews Tone Guides Comparisons Guitarists Beginner Guides About The Guitar Side Toggle Menu Gear Reviews EarthQuaker Devices Hoof Review: Muff-Style Fuzz That Can Actually Cut? By The Guitar Side September 21, 2026 September 21, 2026 The EarthQuaker Devices Hoof makes the most sense if you like what a Big Muff Pi does but keep running into the same problem: the sound is huge alone, then the guitar loses shape the moment the rest of the band comes in. The Hoof keeps the thick sustain and fuzz weight of that general family, but adds one control that changes the whole experience: Shift . Instead of living with one baked-in mid character, you can move the response from more scooped to more mid-forward. That turns the Hoof from “another Muff-inspired fuzz” into a much easier pedal to fit around different amps, guitars and rooms. This EarthQuaker Devices Hoof review focuses on that real-world advantage. If you want a historically exact Russian Muff reproduction, this is not it. If you want the broad idea with more control, more consistency and better mix placement, the Hoof is much easier to justify. In this review Quick verdict Who should buy it? Pros and cons Specs and controls What the Shift control actually does Tone and feel Useful Hoof settings Home, rehearsal and recording Stacking and pedalboard use Hoof vs Big Muff Alternatives Is the Hoof worth it? Hoof FAQ The Hoof is a strong choice if you want Muff-style sustain without being locked into a fixed mid scoop. Its Shift control makes it easier to fit into a band mix, while the germanium/silicon hybrid design keeps the feel smooth and consistent. Skip it if you want raw Fuzz Face cleanup or a strict vintage clone. EarthQuaker Devices Hoof review: who should buy it? Your situation Fit Why You love Muff-style sustain but keep disappearing in a band mix. Strong fit Shift lets you push mids forward instead of accepting a fixed scoop. You move between different amps and need one fuzz that adapts. Strong fit Tone + Shift give you more control over the frequency shape than a classic three-knob Muff. You want dramatic guitar-volume cleanup from almost clean to full fuzz. Mixed It responds, but that is not the main strength of this circuit family. You want an exact vintage Russian Big Muff experience. Look elsewhere The Hoof is inspired by that family but deliberately modernized. Pros and cons Pros Shift control fixes the biggest practical weakness of many Muff-style fuzzes: midrange placement. Germanium/silicon hybrid design balances smooth sustain with modern stability. Wide enough range for gritty lower-gain sounds and heavy saturated fuzz. Works well on guitar and can retain useful low-end definition. More adaptable to different amps than a fixed-voice classic fuzz. Cons If you do not need the Shift control, a simpler Muff-style fuzz may be better value. The extra control means there are more ways to dial a sound that is technically big but badly placed. Not a replacement for a Fuzz Face if cleanup and touch interaction are your priority. Players chasing a very specific vintage Muff version may prefer an actual reissue. How we evaluated this pedal We come at pedals like engineers rather than catalogue writers: circuit architecture first, then control interaction, then how those choices should translate into a real signal chain. With the Hoof, the important variables are the germanium/silicon hybrid design, Tone/Shift interaction, midrange placement and how much definition remains as Fuzz rises. Hard specs and control behavior are cross-checked against EarthQuaker Devices’ current Hoof documentation , then compared with published demos and familiar Muff-style reference circuits. Brief shop or demo-room impressions, when available, are useful as a sanity check but are not presented as long-term ownership. Welcome to your new Hoof™ Fuzz Device! What to say about the Hoof that hasn't already been said? Our flagship fuzz pedal can be found on thousands on pedaboards around the world and has rocked countless stages from stinky suburban basements to Madison Square Garden. Twice. The Hoof is loosely based on the classic green Russian fuzz circuit, and features a hybrid Germanium / Silicon design, pairing maximum tone with maximum temperature stability not found in finicky and expensive vintage units. We hand-match our NOS Germanium transistors to exacting specifications for pedal-to-pedal consistency, taking the guesswork out of your fuzz purchase, and guaranteeing that your Hoof delivers the same smooth, natural, and harmonically rich sustain as all your friends' Hoofs. All your friends have Hoof fuzzes, right? The Hoof has a wide gain range, providing everything from dirty and organic amp-like overdrive, to monstrous fuzz madness. This, paired with the "Shift" control allows you total tonal access, as the "Shift" knob works with the "Tone" control to alter the overall frequency response of the Hoof. Use the "Shift" to boost the highs for a glassy, cutting top-end; use it to cut out some low-mid mud; use it to add some thick stoner rock sludge; use it on bass; use it to combat the muff-style fuzz's notorious "mid scoop;" use it however you'd like, just use it! The Hoof's distinctive, fuzzy character is tight and controlled without sacrificing any "guts," so to speak, so even the gnarliest fuzz tones will sit well in the mix. The Hoof fuzz is all-analog, true bypass, and built one-at-a-time by real life human beans with four fingers and a thumb waiting in line for the horsey rides at the rustic frontierland amusement park of Akron, Ohio, USA. (The Official Center of the Universe) Controls Fuzz: Clockwise for heavy, counterclockwise for light. Tone: Bass to the left, Treble to the right Level: Use this control to make the Hoof louder or quieter. Shift: This adjusts the mid content, clockwise for scooped mids, counterclockwise for boosted. Power Our pedals take a standard 9 volt DC power supply with a 2.1mm negative center barrel. We always recommend pedal-specific, transformer-isolated wall-wart power supplies or multiple isolated- output supplies. Pedals will make extra noise if there is ripple or unclean power. Switching-type power supplies, daisy chains and non-pedal specific power supplies do not filter dirty power as well and let through unwanted noise. Do not run at higher voltages! Current draw 13mA Switching This device is true bypass and uses electronic relay based switching. Audio will not pass without power. © 2017 EarthQuaker Devices LLC. | www.earthquakerdevices.com | info @ earthquakerdevices.com Need help? A two-piece band from Akron, Ohio is playing to a room, and somebody in that room is holding a cell phone up in the air. The video that survives is a smear of early-2000s compression artefacts. You can barely see the stage. But you can hear the guitar, and the guitar is enormous — a fuzz so wide and so structurally load-bearing that the band does not need a bass player, because there is no room left for one. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The guitarist is Dan Auerbach. The pedal doing the damage was built by the band’s then tour manager and sometimes-tech, a guy who had been soldering boxes in his bedroom and who had just decided that his own Russian Big Muff sounded like a wet blanket. His name is Jamie Stillman. The pedal was called the Hoof. Twenty years and several thousand pedals later, EarthQuaker Devices occupies a building on West Bowery Street in Akron with a workforce, a 401k plan and — according to their own account of it — free yoga classes. The Hoof is still in the catalogue, still hand-built in the same city, still four knobs, still sounding like the wall of a barn falling in slow motion. This is the story of how one green-Russian-derived circuit turned a bedroom operation into one of the most recognisable names in American effects, what the pedal actually does, and who has genuinely used one. How to Get the Tone ↓ The short version The EarthQuaker Devices Hoof is a hybrid germanium/silicon fuzz loosely based on the “green Russian” Sovtek-era Big Muff circuit. It has four controls — Fuzz, Tone, Level and Shift — and the Shift control is the entire reason the pedal is not just another Muff clone. It sweeps the midrange from the classic scooped Muff voice to a boosted, cutting, mid-forward voice, which means it can sit in a mix rather than disappearing into one. Current retail is $179 in the US, with the pedal discounted to around $152 at major dealers as of September 2026. It is all-analog, true bypass with relay-based soft switching, draws 15 mA and runs on a standard 9V centre-negative supply. It is not a boutique-scarcity object: EQD have built thousands, and used examples are everywhere. Where it fits: this is the Muff for people who love the sustain and the sludge of a Big Muff Pi but hate what a scooped Muff does to a three-piece band. It is also, unusually for a Muff-family circuit, genuinely good on bass.
